heading: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
text:
Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
[Repository README](../README.md) · [Development setup](setup.md) · [Validation](validation.md) · [Foundation versioning](versioning.md) · [ADR-0014](adr/0014-derive-projects-from-orion-through-git-ancestry-with-recorded-provenance.md) · [ADR-0017](adr/0017-start-derived-projects-from-a-clean-foundation-baseline.md)
This is the practical reference for turning a revision of Orion into a new, independent project and for keeping that project's foundation current: what to decide and provide, how to run the initialization, what the new repository contains, what to do next, and how provenance and foundation upgrades work. [ADR-0014](adr/0014-derive-projects-from-orion-through-git-ancestry-with-recorded-provenance.md) records the ancestry and provenance decision; [ADR-0017](adr/0017-start-derived-projects-from-a-clean-foundation-baseline.md) records the clean-baseline contract. The commands exist in every Orion checkout; the canonical Orion repository itself is never initialized as a project.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Model
text:
Model
The canonical `GabriellMDias/Orion` repository is the upstream development foundation. A derived project is an independent Git repository with its own `origin`, branches, pull requests, CI history, human actions, product decisions, and releases. It starts from a clean clone of Orion and keeps Orion's commit history, so Git can compute what changed upstream and merge it later, but its first commit removes Orion's own reference implementation and development history and gives the repository the project's identity.
Concern
Mechanism
Identity and provenance
[`.orion/project.json`](../.orion/project.json), validated by `pnpm orion:check`
Clean-baseline contract
[`.orion/derivation.json`](../.orion/derivation.json): foundation-only paths, project-owned files and their templates, and the foundation workspace package scope
Immutable starting point
`foundation.initializedFromCommit`: the published Orion commit the project was initialized from; never changes
Current foundation
`foundation.baselineCommit`: the newest Orion commit integrated and validated through a reviewed merge
Canonical upstream
Local remote `orion-upstream`: fetch-only (its push URL is disabled), fetches no tags, and is tracked by no local branch
Product repository
Recorded as `repository.url`; each clone's `origin` is that repository or a fork or mirror of it, never the foundation ([remote rules](#remote-rules))
In the Orion repository the manifest has `"kind": "foundation"` and only describes Orion. A derived project's manifest (schema version 2) has `"kind": "project"` and additionally records its npm `packageScope` and its foundation ancestry. The Living Documentation Portal links source files to the manifest's repository.
A derived project inherits [Apache-2.0-licensed Orion source](../LICENSE). The project remains responsible for licensing its independently created product code and for applicable obligations of inherited and third-party material; Orion's license does not choose the project's overall license.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Prerequisites
text:
Prerequisites
Git with `user.name` and `user.email` configured, Node.js 24.13.0, and pnpm 11.25.0.
A running Testcontainers-compatible container runtime: initialization regenerates the database reference from a migrated PostgreSQL.
Playwright Chromium for the browser tests in `pnpm validate` ([setup](setup.md#prepare-a-clean-checkout)).
A fresh, full clone of Orion that contains no other work. Shallow clones cannot preserve Orion's ancestry.
Permission to create the product repository before publishing. Initialization never contacts the product repository: it creates no repositories and pushes nothing.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Next steps after creation
text:
Next steps after creation
The project's [README](../README.md) routes to its plan and human actions, which track these steps with stable IDs.
**Publish and validate (PH-01, PJ-01).** Push `main` to the new repository and confirm that `pnpm validate` passes locally and that the repository's CI runs.
**Protect the repository (PH-02 to PH-04).** Require pull requests and the `Orion required gate` check on `main`, keep merge commits available for foundation upgrades, enable Renovate, and enable the applicable GitHub security controls. Settings verified for Orion do not apply to the new repository.
**Onboard contributors.** Each clone needs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and the local configuration from [setup](setup.md). Run `pnpm orion:upstream` and `git fetch orion-upstream` in any clone that will inspect or perform foundation upgrades; clones receive no `orion-upstream` remote automatically.
**Define the product (PH-05, PJ-02).** Record the product scope, actors, first capabilities, data classification, and acceptance criteria, then replace the README introduction and current state.
**Build the first module (PJ-03).** Add its schema, reviewed migration, contract, SDK use, web workflow, tests, and documentation as described for [API modules](../apps/api/README.md#modules) and [web modules](../apps/web/README.md#modules), and compose it in `apps/api/src/modules.ts` and `apps/web/src/modules.tsx`. [Orion's reference implementation](#orions-reference-implementation) shows a complete module.
**Replace the placeholder identity (PJ-04).** Replace the brand mark and regenerate the touch icon as described under [web identity](../apps/web/README.md#identity).
**Decide the product license (PH-06)** before distribution requires it.
**Add conditional work when it becomes real (PJ-05).** An identity provider, durable releases, or a deployment environment become new tasks and human actions in the project's own files.
Keep the project's plan and human actions current as work proceeds; `AGENTS.md` routes contributors and agents to them through the README's Current state.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Orion's reference implementation
text:
Orion's reference implementation
The Orion repository composes a complete Approval Request module that demonstrates the architecture from database to browser and is exercised by Orion's validation gate. It is foundation-only: initialization removes it, and no project-owned or shared file refers to it. To study it while building a module, read it in Orion at the commit recorded as the project's baseline, for example in a separate Orion clone or with `git show <baseline>:<path>` after `git fetch orion-upstream`. The paths it occupies are listed in [`.orion/derivation.json`](../.orion/derivation.json). Copy patterns, not the feature: a product module belongs under its own name and is composed in the project's `modules.ts` and `modules.tsx`.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Provenance and foundation upgrades
text:
Provenance and foundation upgrades
Provenance is what makes upgrades possible. Initialization records the Orion commit in both `foundation.initializedFromCommit`, which never changes, and `foundation.baselineCommit`. Because the project keeps Orion's history, Git can compute what changed upstream since the baseline and merge it with a normal three-way merge. Each upgrade merges a newer Orion commit with its history and then records it as the new baseline; `pnpm orion:check` verifies that the baseline is an ancestor of `HEAD`, and `pnpm orion:status` compares it with a fetched `orion-upstream`. The derivation contract travels with every upgrade, and `pnpm orion:prune` reapplies it, so the project stays free of foundation-only content and keeps its own package scope. [Stable semantic tags](versioning.md) make released foundation points easier to identify: a project may be described as derived from a tagged Orion release when its initialization commit matches that tag, while the manifest continues to record the exact commit SHA.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Inspect provenance
text:
Inspect provenance
pnpm orion:status

It prints the project identity and package scope, the initialization and recorded baseline commits, whether `orion-upstream` is configured and fetch-only, and, after `git fetch orion-upstream`, how many upstream commits follow the baseline and whether integrated commits are not yet recorded. It does not fetch or change anything.
`pnpm orion:check` runs in `pnpm validate`.
In Orion, it validates the manifest and derivation contract, requires every foundation-only path and template to exist, and rejects shared tracked files that link to, import, name, or mention foundation-only content. Derivation tooling, ADRs, this guide, and generated output are exempt.
In a project, it validates the manifest and contract, requires the project plan and human actions and the root package name of the recorded scope, rejects any foundation-only path and any remaining reference to the foundation package scope in code or configuration, requires both recorded commits to exist with the initialization commit an ancestor of the baseline and the baseline an ancestor of `HEAD`, and applies the [remote rules](#remote-rules). It needs full history; CI already uses `fetch-depth: 0`.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Remote rules
text:
Remote rules
Git remotes are local configuration, so other clones of the project do not receive `orion-upstream`. Configure it in any clone with:
pnpm orion:upstream
git fetch orion-upstream

Remote
Rule
Enforced by
`origin`
Must not identify the Orion foundation through its fetch or push URL, so product work never has the foundation as its normal push target. It need not equal the project's `repository.url`: contributors may work through a fork or mirror.
`pnpm orion:upstream` refuses; `pnpm orion:check` fails
`orion-upstream`, when present
Its fetch URL must identify the foundation repository recorded in the manifest.
`pnpm orion:upstream` refuses; `pnpm orion:check` fails
`orion-upstream`, when present
Its only push URL must be the disabled `orion-upstream-is-fetch-only`.
`pnpm orion:check` fails and directs you to rerun `pnpm orion:upstream`
`orion-upstream`, when absent
Valid; a normal clone has no foundation remote until a developer configures it.
—
Local branches
No local branch may track `orion-upstream`; an argument-free `git pull` would otherwise merge foundation changes outside a reviewed upgrade.
`pnpm orion:check` fails and directs you to rerun `pnpm orion:upstream`
`pnpm orion:upstream` adds `orion-upstream` from the manifest when absent, replaces every push URL of it with the disabled one, disables its tags, and removes upstream tracking of it from every local branch. It is safe to rerun.
Repository identities compare as normalized HTTPS URLs, so HTTPS, SSH, and scp-like forms of the same repository match. Host names are case-insensitive, but repository path case is significant because self-hosted servers may treat `acme/Ledger` and `acme/ledger` as different repositories: accepting a URL as a given repository, as for `orion-upstream` or the `origin` checked before initialization, requires the exact path. Refusing a URL because it could reach the foundation, as for `origin` or a new project's repository, ignores path case, because hosts such as GitHub resolve differently cased paths to the same repository. An explicit non-default HTTPS port is part of the identity: `https://git.example.com:8443/acme/ledger` differs from `https://git.example.com/acme/ledger`, while `:443` is the same endpoint as no port. A non-default SSH port only selects the SSH transport and does not identify the HTTPS endpoint, so such a URL is refused as a project repository and never matches the foundation; supply the repository's HTTPS URL instead.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Upgrade to a newer Orion revision
text:
Upgrade to a newer Orion revision
An upgrade is a normal reviewable engineering change on a branch. Nothing is applied automatically, and semantic conflicts are resolved by people or agents under review. Tags help humans choose a known release point but do not change this workflow. Ordinary conflicts in project-modified shared files do not by themselves indicate a MAJOR Orion release.
Run `git fetch orion-upstream` and `pnpm orion:status`. Review upstream changes with `git log --oneline <baseline>..orion-upstream/main` and `git diff <baseline> orion-upstream/main`, including ADRs, policies, migrations, tooling, and `.orion/derivation.json`.
Choose the candidate commit; it must be on `orion-upstream/main`. Create a branch, for example `git switch -c orion-upgrade/<short-commit>`, and run `git merge --no-ff <commit>`.
Resolve conflicts in `.orion/project.json`, `.orion/derivation.json`, the release registry, and `package.json` first if they prevent the command from loading. Run `pnpm orion:prune` while other merge conflicts remain. It deletes foundation-only paths the merge changed or added (resolving their modify/delete conflicts), renames foundation package-scope references in resolved shared files, and stages those changes. It leaves unresolved shared files and project-owned files untouched, reports the unresolved paths, and refuses to delete a recorded durable migration or follow linked paths outside the checkout. Resolve and stage reported conflicts, then rerun it.
Resolve remaining conflicts according to [content ownership](#content-ownership): keep the project's version of project-owned files and merge shared files. Never hand-merge generated output: run the generators from step 5, then stage their results (for example `git add -A apps/web/src/generated docs/generated packages/sdk/src/generated`), which resolves conflicts in generated files, including ones the project's output no longer contains. Rerun `pnpm orion:prune` until it reports no unresolved files. Review semantic interactions with product code even where Git reports no conflict.
Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm db:generate`, `pnpm -C apps/api references:write`, `pnpm -C packages/sdk generate`, `pnpm docs:references:write`, and `pnpm validate`. Commit the merge.
Run `pnpm orion:record-baseline <commit>`. It refuses unless the worktree is clean and `orion-upstream` exists and satisfies the [remote rules](#remote-rules). It then fetches `main` from that verified foundation, so refs fetched earlier from another repository cannot vouch for the commit. Finally it requires the commit to be on `orion-upstream/main`, descend from the recorded baseline, and already be an ancestor of `HEAD`. Commit the manifest change, rerun `pnpm validate`, and open the pull request against the project's `main`.
Merge the pull request with a merge commit. Squash or rebase merges discard Orion's commit identities, and `pnpm orion:check` then fails because the recorded baseline is not an ancestor of `HEAD`. The project repository must therefore keep merge commits enabled (project human action PH-02). This applies only to Orion upgrade pull requests.
If the project's default branch requires pull requests, as PH-02 establishes, the merge and baseline update reach `main` together through that pull request. Record the upgrade and any project-specific follow-up in the project plan.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Migrate a project from schema version 1
text:
Migrate a project from schema version 1
Projects initialized before the clean-baseline contract have a schema version 1 manifest with `referenceImplementations`, Orion's plan, human actions, and acceptance report, and usually the Approval Request implementation and `@orion/*` packages. After merging an Orion revision that contains this contract, `pnpm orion:check` refuses the old manifest. Migrate in the upgrade branch:
If the project adopted Approval Request as product behavior, move its code, schema, metadata, grants, and tests out of the foundation-only paths first (for example to `src/features/<product-module>/` and matching paths under the module's own name). Preserve every released migration at its original path and remove that path from the project's `foundationOnly` list in `.orion/derivation.json`; never rename or delete it. Verify uncertain release status under [migration policy](database/migrations.md) before classifying a migration as removable. Only genuinely unreleased reference migrations may be removed or renamed. `orion:prune` refuses removal of recorded durable migrations.
Edit `.orion/project.json`: set `schemaVersion` to `2`, remove `referenceImplementations`, and add `"packageScope": "@<scope>"`.
Run `pnpm orion:prune` to remove foundation-only paths and rename package-scope references.
Replace the project-owned files that still carry Orion's content: render `README.md`, `apps/api/src/modules.ts`, `apps/web/src/modules.tsx`, and the brand assets from the [templates](../.orion/derivation.json) (substituting each `{{PLACEHOLDER}}`), keeping existing project-specific text. Keep `docs/project/`; remove its references to Orion's plan, human actions, acceptance report, and reference implementation, and port the maintenance rules from the plan and human-action templates.
Regenerate as in [upgrade step 5](#upgrade-to-a-newer-orion-revision), run `pnpm validate`, and continue with baseline recording.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Contributing improvements back to Orion
text:
Contributing improvements back to Orion
Product work never goes to `orion-upstream`; its push URL is disabled. To improve the foundation itself, make the change in a separate clone of Orion and submit it there under Orion's own review, then adopt it in projects through the upgrade workflow. Do not move product code, requirements, or history into Orion. In Orion, keep new shared content independent of foundation-only content; extend `.orion/derivation.json` when adding foundation-only or project-owned files.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Limits
text:
Limits
Provenance proves which Orion commits are ancestors of the project; it does not prove that the project still follows every inherited policy. Validation and review remain the enforcement.
`pnpm orion:check` can verify that the recorded baseline is integrated, but only `pnpm orion:status` with a fetched upstream can report newer integrated commits that were not yet recorded.
Upgrades that change foundation-only or project-owned files conflict in projects; projects that diverge heavily from shared files should expect more conflicts there.
The isolation check matches links, imports, path names, and listed terms; it cannot judge whether shared prose implicitly assumes the reference implementation. Review remains necessary.
The immutable Git commit remains the exact foundation revision and provenance identity. [Foundation versioning](versioning.md) assigns human-readable tags only to deliberate stable release points; commits between tags remain usable by SHA.

title: Teluni Product Architecture
heading: Baseline and proposed topology
text:
Baseline and proposed topology
**Implemented foundation:** Node.js/TypeScript ESM, Fastify, PostgreSQL/Prisma infrastructure, TypeBox/OpenAPI and generated TypeScript SDK, React/Vite with TanStack Router/Query, Pino/OpenTelemetry, local validation and CI configuration. [Actual product composition is empty](README.md#verified-baseline). Installed versions are owned by package manifests/lockfile, not this proposal. No new service/library is selected by this document.
**Decided constraints:** use Orion's boundaries; keep a modular backend; support tenants from the first product slice; treat clients and uploaded files as untrusted; avoid premature microservices and distributed infrastructure.
**Proposed:** three product components: an administration web panel, the backend, and a native Android TV player. The initial deployment would serve the panel/API and private media over HTTPS, with PostgreSQL and local persistent media storage on one managed host. The player downloads authorized publications and plays locally. This is a logical topology, not deployed infrastructure.
Component
Responsibility
Trust and persistence boundary
Web panel
Companies, branches, members, devices, media, playlists, schedules, previews, publication, status, operational history; future layouts/campaigns
Untrusted client; generated SDK for API access; no server secrets or direct database/storage access
Backend
Authorization and tenant isolation, domain rules, metadata, media access, publication/sync, schedules, telemetry, audit; future integrations
Owns canonical server state and API contracts; one modular process initially; privileged migrations separate from runtime
Android TV player
Pairing, local configuration, staging, integrity checks, scheduling, playback and bounded diagnostic reporting
Independently distributed untrusted client with its own revocable identity and durable local state; never direct database access
Kotlin, Android Media3/ExoPlayer, and durable local persistence are **proposed** under [ADR-0020](../adr/0020-propose-a-native-android-tv-player.md). Minimum Android/API level, media profiles, persistence library, background behavior, package distribution, and update channels remain pending. No player directory or build system is created in this stage. A future repository placement should make the Android runtime independent; a conceptual name such as `apps/player-android/` is not an existing workspace package. Kotlin must not import TypeScript application internals; HTTP contracts remain interoperable.

text:
Suggested modules and ownership

Owned meaning and entities
Allowed collaboration and phase

`programming`

`publications`

`monitoring`

Consumes device-scoped reports; separates observation freshness from playback success. MVP

Attributable security/publication/lifecycle events across modules
Each capability owns event meaning. Decide persistence/integrity/retention and whether a shared audit component is warranted before extraction; no mandatory generic audit package. MVP

Structured layouts, product/price facts, and promotional lifecycle respectively
Future Phase 3; expose explicit versioned data dependencies to publication

Keep domain rules independent of Fastify, Prisma, filesystem, and providers. The composition root may wire module interfaces; cross-module operations must use explicit public application capabilities with no cycles or arbitrary table writes. Existing `ApiModule` does not automatically provide inter-module authorization or dependency injection. Confirm the narrow composition design when implementing the first collaboration; do not change foundation contracts to match this planning table alone.

title: Teluni Product Architecture
heading: Conceptual entities and relationships
text:
Conceptual entities and relationships
This is a domain model for review, not a database schema, migration, wire contract, or generated reference.
Entity
Relationship and invariant
Platform
Operates customer companies; platform operational authority is distinct from tenant membership
Company
Tenant ownership boundary for branches, members, media, programming, devices and publications
Branch
Belongs to one company; holds local business timezone/settings and assigned devices
User / membership
A human identity can have explicitly authorized memberships; a membership binds a user to a company and permitted branch scope
Device / enrollment session
A device belongs to one company and branch after pairing; enrollment is temporary and single-use; reassignment requires safe unlink/clear semantics
Media asset / stored object
Tenant-owned metadata points to a validated immutable file version; storage location is not authorization
Playlist / item
Company-owned ordered references to eligible media with duration semantics; edits produce draft changes
Schedule / assignment
Associates eligible programming with a device and local-time rule; all references share tenant and permitted branch scope
Publication / manifest
Immutable validated snapshot of programming, assets and interpretation version; references remain resolvable through retention
Device publication state
Separates desired, staged, active and last-reported versions per device; acknowledgement is not proof of continuous playback
Device report / audit event
Observation belongs to a tenant/device; attributable action evidence has independent integrity and retention requirements
**Future:** a layout has versioned structured components/regions and reusable assets; a catalog product has description/images/category/availability and normal/promotional price facts, with combo support; a campaign connects promotional intent, validity and priority to programming/publications. A product-price update must eventually update dependent published content without manual artwork recreation. Decide controlled version propagation and caching before implementation; editing mutable data behind an immutable publication is not an implied solution.
Tenant IDs must participate in ownership validation for references and uniqueness. The physical enforcement choice (including compound constraints and possible row-level security) is [ADR-0018](../adr/0018-propose-tenant-owned-data-in-the-modular-backend.md), still proposed. IDs supplied by the caller never establish authority.

title: Teluni Product Architecture
heading: Publication and integration boundaries
text:
Publication and integration boundaries
[Playback/sync](playback-and-sync.md) owns publication consistency and recovery. Candidate HTTP operations must follow existing [API principles](../api/principles.md), [error contract](../api/error-contract.md), [API versioning](../api/versioning.md), and [delivery policy](../architecture/delivery-and-side-effects.md). No endpoint paths, payload schemas, protocol version numbers, jobs, broker, WebSocket, S3 provider, CDN, or Kotlin client generator are selected here. Polling/reconciliation is a candidate; notification transport remains D-04.
**Future:** an externally consumable documented API should allow authorized partners to update product/price data from ERP/POS systems, with stable generated OpenAPI documentation, scoped machine identities, rate limits, versioning, and safe retry/webhook semantics. Documentation must be usable by partner companies without private repository access. The current internal living portal is not proof of a public integration service. Integrations must pass application authorization and validation; no direct ERP database coupling.

title: Teluni Human Actions
heading: Purpose and current state
text:
Purpose and current state
This checklist records Teluni's prerequisites that require a project-owner decision, a human-controlled account action, an unavailable privilege, or securely supplied external configuration. Every contributor or coding agent performing implementation work must maintain it and must never silently skip work because human intervention is needed.
Teluni (https://github.com/GabriellMDias/teluni) was initialized from Orion (https://github.com/GabriellMDias/Orion). Repository settings verified for Orion—Renovate, branch protection, and security controls—do not apply to this repository; the actions below establish them here. Conditional needs such as an identity provider, durable releases, or a deployment environment become new actions when their trigger occurs.

title: Teluni Human Actions
heading: Maintaining this checklist
text:
Maintaining this checklist
Inspect existing decisions, access, tools, configuration, and prior authorization before requesting human intervention. Complete authorized automation and all useful preparation first.
Keep one stable `PH-NN` ID per coherent action; never reuse or renumber IDs. Split broad items into independently verifiable actions as they become concrete, and add newly discovered actions immediately.
Every action retains its ID, checkbox, owner, status, dependency, and evidence. Active or conditional requests also need the exact action, reason, non-secret configuration names, and verification method. Use `pending`, `in progress`, `completed`, `blocked`, or `changed` consistently with the [plan](implementation-plan.md#maintaining-this-plan).
Before asking the user, provide a concrete request: the exact setting or decision, prepared options where appropriate, why automation cannot finish it, affected task IDs, and how completion will be checked.
If an action blocks work now, mark the dependent plan task `blocked`, link this entry, and surface the request to the user. Continue independent authorized work.
Use `[x]` and `completed` only after verification, recording safe evidence and the verification date. If direct verification is unavailable, record the limitation rather than claiming success.
Reopen an action with `[ ]` if later evidence invalidates completion, access expires, or configuration changes, and record why.
A conditional item that becomes unnecessary remains `[ ]` with status `changed`, an explicit reason, and its future trigger or replacement.

title: Teluni Human Actions
heading: Safe configuration handoff
text:
Safe configuration handoff
Record configuration names, required scopes, environment, purpose, non-secret resource identifiers, and secure destination. Never record passwords, tokens, API keys, connection strings containing credentials, private keys, or complete environment dumps here, in the plan, in chat, or in tracked example files.
Name only implemented configuration keys and link the [generated configuration reference](../generated/configuration/api.md); do not invent variable names in advance.
Humans place secrets directly into the selected protected secret store or an explicitly documented ignored local file. Contributors verify presence and authorized behavior without printing secret contents.
Use synthetic local and test data and ephemeral credentials where possible. Production secrets must not be prerequisites for ordinary development or CI.

Teluni was initialized on 2026-10-17 from Orion commit `53bcc705a9f68f01aa1bbea3a0f4df4a009577ea` of https://github.com/GabriellMDias/Orion. The [project manifest](../../.orion/project.json) records that immutable initialization commit and the Orion baseline currently integrated. Results recorded for the Orion repository are not results for this repository until they pass in this checkout and in this repository's CI.

title: Teluni Implementation Plan
heading: Maintaining this plan
text:
Maintaining this plan
Every contributor or coding agent performing implementation work must maintain this plan and the [project human actions](human-actions.md) within the user's authorized scope.
Before implementation, inspect actual repository state, the relevant task, its prerequisites, governing policy, and linked human actions. Do not treat a planned capability or unchecked action as available.
Mark a task `in progress` when work actually starts. Update statuses when evidence, scope, dependencies, or blockers change, and before each handoff or completion report.
Allocate stable task IDs as `PJ-NN`; never reuse or renumber them. Add finer tasks when needed; do not hide unfinished subtasks inside a completed row.
Record concise evidence in the task row: implementation paths, validation commands and results, review references, or a linked decision. Record evidence produced for this repository—local validation, this repository's CI runs, and this repository's external settings. Do not store secret values or sensitive output.
A task becomes `completed` only when its deliverables and acceptance criteria are satisfied with evidence. A partial implementation or an unavailable required check is not completion.
When human intervention is necessary, add or update a project human action, link it from the affected task, mark that task `blocked`, and tell the user what is needed. Continue independent authorized work where possible.
A future prerequisite is `pending`, not automatically `blocked`.
When scope or sequencing changes, use `changed`, explain why and what replaces the work, and link supporting decisions. Do not delete unresolved obligations to make the plan look complete.
Update command availability, current documentation, generated artifacts, and the human actions in the same coherent change where applicable. Do not change ADR status merely to record implementation progress.
Status
Meaning
`pending`
Not started; includes conditional work whose trigger has not occurred.
`in progress`
Work has started and is incomplete.
`completed`
Applicable deliverables and acceptance criteria are satisfied with evidence.
`blocked`
The identified work cannot proceed without a recorded dependency, decision, access, or correction.
`changed`
Scope, applicability, or sequencing was explicitly revised; reason and replacement or disposition are recorded.

title: Teluni MVP Requirements and Acceptance
heading: Scope and acceptance rules
text:
Scope and acceptance rules
**Decided:** the MVP must complete the company-to-screen journey for images and videos, including offline Android TV playback and basic monitoring. All capabilities below are requirements, not implemented functionality. Functional requirements reflect the owner's brief; proposed policies and quantitative targets are identified separately. This document owns scope and observable acceptance; the [plan](implementation-plan.md) owns delivery status.
ID
Functional requirement
Required acceptance evidence before pilot release
FR-01
Companies, branches, users, company settings, authentication, and basic permissions
Two synthetic companies each have a branch and users. Authorized members can manage their allowed resources. Direct API attempts, lists, search, media access, and identifier substitution cannot cross company/branch scope. Disabled/revoked access is rejected within the agreed freshness policy.
FR-02
Device identity, temporary-code pairing, company/branch assignment, per-device name/configuration, safe unlink
A code displayed by an unpaired player is claimed by an authorized user once. Expired/replayed codes, concurrent claims, wrong-scope assignment, and revoked identities fail safely. Reassignment cannot expose the previous tenant's content or credentials.
FR-03
Horizontal/vertical orientation where supported
An approved pilot device displays supported orientations correctly. Unsupported hardware/settings produce a clear capability response, not a silent claim of support.
FR-04
Image/video upload, validation, identification, organization, metadata, reuse, reference-aware deletion
Approved file profiles upload and play on tested hardware; spoofed type, malformed/oversized content, and unauthorized reads are rejected. Reused media can appear in multiple playlists. A referenced or active-version asset cannot be physically removed unsafely.
FR-05
Playlist editing, ordered items, duration, continuous repetition, device assignment, basic transitions where supported
Reordering is deterministic; configured image duration and video-duration policy are reflected in previews and playback. A loop continues across repeated items. An unsupported transition is handled by a declared baseline behavior.
FR-06
Scheduling by start/end date, local time, weekday, and recurrence, with explicit conflict and no-match rules
Preview and player agree for ordinary windows, overlapping/empty windows, overnight windows, recurrence, expiry, and timezone transitions. Invalid/conflicting schedules cannot result in accidental mixed or undefined output.
FR-07
Preview, explicit publication, immutable versions, device synchronization, last-valid-version preservation
Draft edits do not change active displays. Publishing requires authorization and validation of a complete version. Repeated/concurrent requests have defined results. Incomplete or corrupt staging never replaces the last valid active version.
FR-08
Android TV player and continuous offline reproduction
A paired, fully synchronized approved device loops its local programming without streaming normal video from the backend, through the agreed outage duration, reboot, and recovery scenarios in [playback acceptance](playback-and-sync.md#failure-and-recovery-acceptance).
FR-09
Online/offline indication, last communication, app version, free storage, sync state, relevant failures
Scoped panel views show observed timestamps and version states. Lost connectivity becomes stale/offline under a documented threshold; reconnection reconciles actual state. Authorization or download failure is distinguishable from current playback failure.
Group-based playlist assignment is a desired extension of FR-05, but the brief also places device groups in enterprise evolution. **Proposed MVP boundary:** direct assignment to individual devices; no separate reusable group-management capability. This scope resolution remains [D-06](architecture.md#pending-decisions). Campaign management is similarly reserved for Phase 3; scheduled playlists provide the MVP promotion use case.

title: Teluni MVP Requirements and Acceptance
heading: Proposed behavior requiring confirmation
text:
Proposed behavior requiring confirmation
These are candidate policies for validation under [PH-09](human-actions.md#ph-09), not silently accepted business rules:
One customer company is one tenant; branches belong to exactly one company. Multi-company access is explicit membership, not an implicit platform privilege.
Company enrollment starts with an attributable platform-admin action and an initial company admin; public self-service signup/invitations and approval flows are pending identity design.
Use a continuous default playlist for each assigned device and reject overlapping active schedule windows for that device in the MVP. When no window matches, play the declared default. When no valid program has ever been installed, display a safe local setup/no-content state. An expired promotion must not become an implicit fallback.
A schedule's end is exclusive; overnight windows, recurrence, daylight-saving ambiguity, and long-offline clock uncertainty need an explicit interpretation before contracts are written.
Manual image duration and video completion form the initial baseline; clipping, early interruption, and mixed-duration rules require hardware validation. Basic cuts are the candidate transition baseline.
Physical deletion of media referenced by a draft or retained publication is rejected with reference information scoped to the caller. Marking/archive and eventual garbage collection must account for retained player versions; retention periods are pending.
The unlink policy must distinguish stopping future access, locally clearing data when the device reconnects, and the inability to erase a disconnected device remotely. Decide the permitted offline playback interval after revocation under D-03.

title: Teluni MVP Requirements and Acceptance
heading: Release acceptance journey
text:
Release acceptance journey
Provision two isolated synthetic companies, branch-scoped operators, and a supported Android TV device. Verify allowed and denied actions at the API and media boundary.
Pair the device, upload approved images/videos, build a playlist and schedules, preview them, and explicitly publish version A. Confirm desired, downloaded, and active versions are distinguishable.
Exercise draft changes and publish B while playback continues. Cut network/power at staging and activation boundaries, restore operation, and verify a complete A or B is used, never a mixed generation.
Exercise the scheduling boundary and no-match/conflict rules offline, including timezone and clock failure cases.
Reconnect, reconcile status, revoke/unlink, and test re-enrollment according to the agreed offline revocation policy.
Rehearse a PostgreSQL-plus-media restore and endpoint migration in an isolated environment. Have a nontechnical pilot operator complete the core workflow and record costs and failures.
Evidence must include automated contract/security/integration/browser tests, real hardware/power/network tests, restore results, and pilot observation. Work may be implemented incrementally; a usable pilot requires the complete applicable acceptance set.

text:
Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
[Project documentation](README.md) · [Risks](risks.md) · [ADR-0021 proposal](../adr/0021-propose-a-single-host-pilot-with-portable-persistent-storage.md)

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Constraints and current state
text:
Constraints and current state
**Decided constraint:** no present cloud-service budget. The owner intends to use a personal residential server for development, tests and potentially initial customers, moving to a VPS/cloud when revenue or operational need justifies it. **Proposed technology:** Debian Linux, Docker Compose, a reverse proxy with HTTPS, local persistent media, automated backups and suitable monitoring. None is a deployed Teluni environment or executable procedure in this repository.
Follow inherited [production access](../security/production-access.md), [secrets management](../security/secrets-management.md), [retention](../security/data-retention.md), [observability](../reliability/observability.md), [alerting](../reliability/alerting.md), and [runbook authoring](../runbooks/authoring.md). This plan does not grant production authority. Write tested deployment/recovery runbooks when the environment exists, rather than speculative commands now.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Residential exposure and readiness gate
text:
Residential exposure and readiness gate
[PH-10](human-actions.md#ph-10) requires an actual host/network inventory: CPU/RAM/disk and growth, upload bandwidth, data caps, power/reboot recovery, router/firewall, public address or CGNAT, ISP restrictions, available domain, certificate renewal, secure remote administration and backup connectivity. Keep private addresses, credentials and sensitive topology out of tracked public documentation.
A tunnel, free DNS option or any video-delivery intermediary requires evaluation of current terms, limits, privacy, security, transfer cost and failure behavior before selection. Do not assume Cloudflare Tunnel, DNS, or video distribution automatically provides an acceptable production path. No such provider is selected here.
Before any real pilot, record and demonstrate:
HTTPS works end to end; only intentional public application endpoints are exposed. PostgreSQL, orchestration dashboards and administrative interfaces remain private/restricted. Remote administration does not imply an unrestricted remote-control product feature.
Development/test and customer data, identities, credentials and backups are separated; logs/diagnostics are redacted; real data does not enter development fixtures.
Durable database and media survive container recreation, controlled app updates and host reboot. Schema migrations use reviewed release procedures and an explicit recovery plan.
Offline playback has been tested independently from backend availability. A home outage still prevents new uploads, publication, pairing, current monitoring and some recovery; communicate these limits to pilot participants.
The owner agrees measurable availability, maintenance, incident contact, backup RPO/RTO and support expectations. No commercial SLA is implied by the architecture.
Until verified, external exposure and real-customer operation are **pending**, even if development works locally.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Persistent state and storage portability
text:
Persistent state and storage portability
Keep environment-specific URLs, credentials and paths in validated environment configuration; use only implemented keys from the [configuration reference](../generated/configuration/api.md) today. Define and document new keys with their future canonical schemas when implemented. Do not embed the residential hostname/path in business entities, contracts or player binaries.
**Proposed storage boundary:** the media capability owns object identity, integrity, metadata, authorized reads and lifecycle. Isolate the actual filesystem I/O behind a cohesive media-owned storage responsibility so a future S3-compatible implementation can preserve object semantics without rewriting domain rules. Avoid a general provider framework or mandatory S3 dependency now. Object-store replacement still needs verified access, integrity, migration and concurrency semantics; portability is not a free automatic migration.
Use durable logical object identifiers rather than storing temporary download credentials as business identity. External media endpoints are configurable. Authorized delivery may use an API or another reviewed access mechanism; public filesystem paths and unbounded permanent bearer URLs are not the default.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Backup and restore requirements
text:
Backup and restore requirements
Backups must cover PostgreSQL, media and the non-secret configuration/release metadata needed to reconstruct operation. Protect and recover secrets through a separate controlled process. A database-only backup is insufficient if it points to unavailable media.
Choose a consistency method for the database-plus-files set, backup schedule, off-host destination, encryption/key recovery, retention, capacity and success/failure reporting. A second directory on the same disk does not cover loss of the host. Local budget constraints do not eliminate the need to resolve off-host recovery before accepting private customer data.
Rehearse restore into an isolated environment: verify migration/application compatibility, ownership/permissions, manifest-to-file integrity, representative playback and tenant access, then reconcile revoked identities and deletion/retention obligations. Record achieved recovery point/time and compare them with owner-approved RPO/RTO. Preserve audit/release history; do not restore stale authorization silently.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Future host or storage migration
text:
Future host or storage migration
**Proposed sequence**, to turn into tested runbooks once topology and credentials exist:
Inventory supported player versions, configurable API/media addresses, tenant data, assets, release versions and secret destinations. Prepare DNS/certificate ownership and compatible software at the destination.
Rehearse backup restore and file verification without customer writes. Determine whether logical object IDs remain stable and how private media authorization is preserved.
Plan a bounded write cutover or verified incremental reconciliation to avoid divergent metadata and media. Preserve audit and device identities without exposing their credentials.
Update endpoints through the approved mechanism with certificate validation and rollback capability. Keep the old address/redirect or compatibility path only for an explicitly defined overlap, accounting for long-offline players. Never accept arbitrary redirected credential recipients.
Verify representative players reconnect, reconcile desired/active versions, and continue offline playback. Check uploads, access denial, publication, backups and monitoring on the new host.
Close the rollback window deliberately, reconcile retained data/deletions and retire old storage/credentials safely. The endpoint overlap and maximum supported offline interval must be compatible; unresolved unreachable devices require a support plan.
Triggers for migration include measured cost/availability/support risk, storage or uplink saturation, growth, or earned revenue supporting operations. Cloud procurement and live migration are outside this documentation task.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
text:
Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
[Project documentation](README.md) · [MVP acceptance](mvp.md) · [ADR-0019 proposal](../adr/0019-propose-immutable-publications-and-atomic-player-activation.md)

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Required guarantees and proposal boundary
text:
Required guarantees and proposal boundary
**Decided requirements:** normal playback uses local images/videos, continues during temporary server/network outages, validates new content, activates a complete programming version, and preserves the last valid programming for recovery. Streaming every playback from the backend is not the normal delivery model.
**Proposed mechanism:** an immutable versioned manifest, durable staged downloads and an atomic local active-generation reference. The exact format, integrity algorithm/metadata, local transaction/storage technique, synchronization transport, and protocol compatibility window remain D-04/D-07. This is not an implemented protocol. Follow [delivery/retry policy](../architecture/delivery-and-side-effects.md), [compatibility](../architecture/versioning-and-compatibility.md), and [file/identity security](security-and-i18n.md).

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Publication lifecycle
text:
Publication lifecycle
An authorized administrator previews draft playlist/schedule state and deliberately publishes. Draft edits cannot change an already active publication.
The backend validates tenant/branch references, supported asset profiles, scheduling rules, targets and media availability. It creates a complete immutable snapshot and records the desired version durably. A publication must not be announced as available before required assets and metadata are durable.
A device authenticates independently and reconciles its desired version with local staged/active state. It obtains only its authorized tenant/assignment data and compatible manifests.
It computes missing/changed assets, checks the space budget including staging and retained fallback, and downloads with bounded timeouts/retries. A retry may refresh authorized download access without making assets public.
It validates file length/integrity and player compatibility before treating an asset as usable. Interrupted partial files cannot masquerade as complete assets. A checksum detects corruption; it does not authenticate an untrusted manifest by itself.
It prepares the complete local schedule/resources and durably switches the active generation only when all required resources are usable. The exact safe playback boundary for the switch needs hardware tests; an in-place overwrite is not acceptable.
It reports receipt, staging and activation separately. Lost/repeated acknowledgements must be reconcilable. Backend intent and device observation must remain distinct in the panel.
It retains the previous valid generation for recovery under the selected capacity/retention policy. Garbage collection never removes active, staged, or retained recovery resources. Failed publication does not destroy the current generation.
Candidate logical states are `unpaired`, `no-content`, `staging`, `ready`, `active`, and `degraded`; these are design vocabulary, not committed enum/API names. A device can actively play A while staging B and reporting a failed download. Monitoring must represent these concurrent facts rather than presenting every synchronization error as a playback outage.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Consistency and concurrency
text:
Consistency and concurrency
Repeated publication/download/acknowledgement requests need explicit retry/idempotency semantics. Concurrent publishers must detect stale drafts or conflicting target changes; a successful old sync must not silently overwrite a newer desired assignment.
The manifest includes enough information to bind assets and rules to one generation and declare the supported interpretation. Content paths alone are not stable identity if file contents can change underneath them.
The proposed target is the latest authorized compatible desired generation; whether to skip intermediate versions needs confirmation for scheduled content and audit requirements. Do not use device wall-clock order as publication identity.
PostgreSQL commits and media filesystem writes are not one transaction. Stage/verify durable objects, then commit references/intent with a recoverable cleanup/reconciliation design. An in-memory after-commit callback alone is insufficient for required distribution.
Initial synchronization needs backend access; offline-first is not offline initial pairing. With no installed valid programming, show a safe setup/no-content screen without private tenant details.
Restoring a retained generation must still respect campaign validity and schedule fallback rules. A rollback cannot resurrect expired offers merely because their files exist.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Time and scheduling
text:
Time and scheduling
The schedule must carry the agreed business timezone and unambiguous interpretation. The backend preview and player must share contract fixtures for weekday recurrence, date boundaries, overnight intervals, daylight-saving gaps/overlaps, and device timezone override. Store/compare instants and preserve the timezone needed to interpret recurring local-time rules; do not infer a business timezone from the server host.
Keep retry elapsed-time calculations separate from business wall-clock scheduling. Detect unreasonable device clock changes and report uncertainty. A manifest's validity window, default program and tolerated clock uncertainty must determine safe offline output. The exact policy for expiry and prolonged disconnection is **pending**, not an unlimited license to display stale prices/promotions.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Failure and recovery acceptance
text:
Failure and recovery acceptance
Condition
Required observable outcome
Server/network outage after synchronization
Last valid local program continues for the agreed offline envelope; schedule expiry/default behavior follows the approved rules
Interrupted download or expired download authorization
Retry safely/resume only when supported and verified; never activate a partial file; current playback continues
Corrupt/unsupported manifest or media
Reject staging with a bounded actionable reason; preserve active generation; avoid infinite hot retry loops
Insufficient disk/memory or unavailable media path
Refuse unsafe staging, report capacity failure; preserve active/recovery assets; no unbounded downloads or deletion of active content
Reboot, process crash, power loss during download/switch
Recover durable active/staging state; play a complete valid generation; reconcile orphan partial files without corrupting the active set
Duplicate requests/acknowledgements or rapid publications
Idempotent/reconcilable outcomes; no mixed generations, cross-tenant references, or rollback caused by stale acknowledgement
Schedule conflict, no match, expired promotion, clock drift
Approved deterministic validation/fallback/uncertainty policy; no unintended expired commercial content
Revoked or unlinked device
Server rejects new protected operations; local playback/erasure follows the explicit disconnected-revocation policy; never claim remote erasure while unreachable
Incompatible backend/player generation
Reject safely or use a supported compatible version according to the documented support matrix; no forced interpretation of an unknown schema
Player update failure or endpoint migration
Recover supported playback/local data and connection configuration; do not make an untested app rollback or credential leak the recovery path
Record tests for each interruption boundary on representative hardware, not just happy-path mocks. Quantitative outage, retry, storage, startup and recovery targets are [PH-09](human-actions.md#ph-09); hardware and update constraints are [PH-08](human-actions.md#ph-08). No power-failure durability claim is made before evidence.

Origin and pilot
The initial opportunity is a snack bar considering televisions for products, images, videos, and promotions. It is a candidate pilot, not a confirmed customer or an exclusive definition of the product.

Actors and core journeys

title: Teluni Product Vision
heading: Commercial hypotheses
text:
Commercial hypotheses
**Decided:** recurring SaaS is the intended business model. **Proposed:** charge primarily by number of screens, potentially with a company minimum and feature-based plans. BRL 79.90/month for up to two screens is an exploratory price only, not an approved offer, entitlement, tax treatment, or billing rule.
Prices, plans, storage/traffic/processing limits, support hours, installation fees, cancellation, costs, and partner/referral arrangements require [PH-12](human-actions.md#ph-12). The snack bar pilot should provide evidence of usability, reliability, support demand, willingness to pay, and actual costs. Automatic billing and payment-gateway integration are **future**, not MVP prerequisites. International currencies and presentation follow the [localization requirements](security-and-i18n.md#internationalization).
There is currently no cloud-service budget. Residential hosting is an entry proposal with explicit [operational gates and risks](operations.md), not a commitment to production availability.

text:
Meaning of status
Product/design status
Meaning
**Decided**
A product requirement or inherited accepted direction agreed for planning. It does not mean implemented.

A candidate solution or acceptance policy requiring evaluation/review. New ADRs remain `proposed` under the [ADR process](../adr/authoring.md).

title: Teluni Product Documentation
heading: Verified baseline
text:
Verified baseline
The [manifest](../../.orion/project.json) identifies a derived Teluni project, initialized from Orion commit `53bcc705a9f68f01aa1bbea3a0f4df4a009577ea`. [API composition](../../apps/api/src/modules.ts) is empty; [web composition](../../apps/web/src/modules.tsx) contains the core shell/portal only. There are no product tables/migrations, player application, media service, deployment manifests, or tenant workflows. The API runtime has health routes, configuration, telemetry, PostgreSQL infrastructure, and optional JWT access-token verification. These are foundation capabilities, not a working SaaS sign-in or tenant system.
This documentation stage does not authorize implementation, deployment, external publication, or acquisition of paid services. The [plan](implementation-plan.md#phase-sequence-and-exit-criteria) identifies the next review and delivery gates.
